lists.title: Privacy notice
lists.what: What your privacy notice must tell people, when you collect their data from them.

items.text: the identity and the contact details of the controller and, where applicable, of the controller's representative;
items.plain: Who you are and how to contact you (and your EU representative, if you have one).

items.text: the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable;
items.plain: How to contact your data protection officer, if you have one.

items.text: the purposes of the processing for which the personal data are intended as well as the legal basis for the processing;
items.plain: Why you use the data, and the legal basis for each purpose.

items.text: where the processing is based on point (f) of Article 6(1), the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party;
items.plain: If you rely on legitimate interests: what those interests are.

items.text: the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any;
items.plain: Who receives the data (by name or by type).

items.text: where applicable, the fact that the controller intends to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation and the existence or absence of an adequacy decision by the Commission, or in the case of transfers referred to in Article 46 or 47, or the second subparagraph of Article 49(1), reference to the appropriate or suitable safeguards and the means by which to obtain a copy of them or where they have been made available.
items.plain: Whether the data leaves the EEA, and what protects it there.

items.text: the period for which the personal data will be stored, or if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period;
items.plain: How long you keep the data, or how you decide.

items.text: the existence of the right to request from the controller access to and rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing concerning the data subject or to object to processing as well as the right to data portability;
items.plain: The rights people have: access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection and portability.

items.text: where the processing is based on point (a) of Article 6(1) or point (a) of Article 9(2), the existence of the right to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal;
items.plain: If you rely on consent: that it can be withdrawn at any time.

items.text: the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority;
items.plain: That people can complain to a data protection authority.

items.text: whether the provision of personal data is a statutory or contractual requirement, or a requirement necessary to enter into a contract, as well as whether the data subject is obliged to provide the personal data and of the possible consequences of failure to provide such data;
items.plain: Whether people must give the data (by law or contract), and what happens if they don’t.

items.text: the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, referred to in Article 22(1) and (4) and, at least in those cases, meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject.
items.plain: Any automated decisions or profiling, the logic behind them and what they mean for the person.

items.text: the categories of personal data concerned;
items.plain: Only if you got the data from someone else: the types of data you hold.

items.text: from which source the personal data originate, and if applicable, whether it came from publicly accessible sources;
items.plain: Only if you got the data from someone else: where it came from, including public sources.

lists.title: Processor contract
lists.what: What the contract with a company that handles personal data for you must say.

items.text: Processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law, that is binding on the processor with regard to the controller and that sets out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of data subjects and the obligations and rights of the controller. That contract or other legal act shall stipulate, in particular, that the processor:
items.plain: The contract describes the subject and length of the work, what is done and why, the types of data and people, and your rights and duties.

items.text: processes the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which the processor is subject; in such a case, the processor shall inform the controller of that legal requirement before processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest;
items.plain: They act only on your written instructions, including on sending data outside the EU.

items.text: ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality;
items.plain: Their staff are bound to keep the data confidential.

items.text: takes all measures required pursuant to Article 32;
items.plain: They take the security measures required by Article 32.

items.text: respects the conditions referred to in paragraphs 2 and 4 for engaging another processor;
items.plain: They use sub-processors only with your permission, and pass on the same duties.

items.text: taking into account the nature of the processing, assists the controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising the data subject's rights laid down in Chapter III;
items.plain: They help you answer requests from people about their data.

items.text: assists the controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to Articles 32 to 36 taking into account the nature of processing and the information available to the processor;
items.plain: They help you with security, breaches, impact assessments and consulting the regulator.

items.text: at the choice of the controller, deletes or returns all the personal data to the controller after the end of the provision of services relating to processing, and deletes existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the personal data;
items.plain: At the end, they delete or return all the data, as you choose.

items.text: makes available to the controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in this Article and allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or another auditor mandated by the controller.
items.plain: They give you what you need to show compliance, and allow audits and inspections.

lists.title: Records of processing
lists.what: What your record of processing activities must contain (as a controller).

items.text: the name and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the joint controller, the controller's representative and the data protection officer;
items.plain: Your name and contact details, and those of any joint controller, representative and data protection officer.

items.text: the purposes of the processing;
items.plain: The purposes of the processing.

items.text: a description of the categories of data subjects and of the categories of personal data;
items.plain: The types of people and the types of data.

items.text: the categories of recipients to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed including recipients in third countries or international organisations;
items.plain: Who receives the data, including anyone outside the EU.

items.text: where applicable, transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, including the identification of that third country or international organisation and, in the case of transfers referred to in the second subparagraph of Article 49(1), the documentation of suitable safeguards;
items.plain: Any transfers outside the EEA, and the safeguards where needed.

items.text: where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data;
items.plain: Where possible, when each type of data will be deleted.

items.text: where possible, a general description of the technical and organisational security measures referred to in Article 32(1).
items.plain: Where possible, a general description of your security measures.

lists.after: Organisations with fewer than 250 employees are exempt only for occasional processing that is not likely to be risky and does not involve special categories or criminal data (Article 30(5)).

lists.title: Breach report
lists.what: What your report to the data protection authority must contain at least.

items.text: describe the nature of the personal data breach including where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects concerned and the categories and approximate number of personal data records concerned;
items.plain: What happened, and roughly how many people and records are involved, and of what kind.

items.text: communicate the name and contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point where more information can be obtained;
items.plain: Who to contact for more information (your DPO or another contact).

items.text: describe the likely consequences of the personal data breach;
items.plain: The likely consequences for the people.

items.text: describe the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the controller to address the personal data breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects.
items.plain: What you have done or will do about it, including to limit the harm.

items.text: The controller shall document any personal data breaches, comprising the facts relating to the personal data breach, its effects and the remedial action taken. That documentation shall enable the supervisory authority to verify compliance with this Article.
items.plain: Keep your own record of every breach, even the ones you do not report.

lists.after: Use the Response timeline to count your 72 hours.

lists.title: Do you need a DPIA?
lists.what: A data protection impact assessment is always required in these three cases (Article 35(3)); national lists add more.

items.text: a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person;
items.plain: You evaluate people systematically and extensively by automated means, including profiling, and decide things that affect them legally or similarly.

items.text: processing on a large scale of special categories of data referred to in Article 9(1), or of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10; or
items.plain: You process special categories of data, or criminal records, on a large scale.

items.text: a systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale.
items.plain: You monitor a publicly accessible area systematically and on a large scale (for example, CCTV of a street).

lists.after: Tick any that apply: one is enough to require an assessment. Each country’s authority also publishes its own list of processing that needs one (Article 35(4)).
